summary.en: Hear a percentage as a number plus a fixed expression.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 6.

The season 1 finale mentions *Dix pour cent du cachet d'une star*. The show's title is also a practical expression: *dix* supplies the number and *pour cent* names the percentage unit.

Learn *pour cent* together rather than treating *pour* as an isolated word with its usual short gloss. After the percentage, *du cachet* identifies the amount on which the share is based. *du* combines *de + le* here; it does not independently mean an unspecified quantity.

The final phrase *d'une star* further specifies whose fee is being discussed. A short line can therefore contain several nested relationships even when most of its words are small.

On replay, separate the number, the percentage expression and the amount being divided. This is a useful way to recognise the meaning of the show's name inside an ordinary business conversation.
